fixed.item: breakages.json (tools_vehicles, G7): this domain's share of the P1 gate's substep-cost regression, +0.06 ms (tools_vehicles.disposals 0.001 -> 0.024, leaks)
fixed.how: Two causes, both removed with every result unchanged. (1) fixes.disposal_system ran _hard_in_hopper (w.children: a scan of every entity) for every disposal on every substep, switched off or not; it now runs only after the live check (an off plate reads nothing from the hopper, so the order is exact): disposals 0.027 -> 0.001 ms. (2) The kernel's read views (review M3) made every static-index build ~3x dearer (first-substep builds 0.024 -> 0.055 ms per substep, the 300 s systems' first runs 0.009 -> 0.017): every index predicate now declares its reads (common.index_reads -> World.static_index reads=), and the 16 indexes a system, idle probe or invariant looks up every substep/step are registered with common.per_step_index and built by common._prebuild_indexes at episode_start (order -90, before any hook writes), where the World evaluates them on the plain records (1.4-2.0 ms per house vs 3.7-5.4 ms for the same builds through views mid-step). water_fixtures and heat_sources (action/overflow lookups) stay lazy. Exactness: an index's content is a pure function of the state; state digests of 12 cases (gen-1 seeds 0-5, gen-2 seeds 0-3, realistic+geometric seeds 0 and 1; after reset, after the bench's 40-substep loop and after a 1 h wait) are identical to the phase-1 code's (scratch digests.py, dig_base.txt / dig_new.txt).
